thread.title: Giovanni Leoni is on the cusp of a return to a Liverpool defence that looks futureproof
thread.title_full: Giovanni Leoni is on the cusp of a return to a Liverpool defence that looks futureproof

author: Gregg Evans
title: Giovanni Leoni is on the cusp of a return to a Liverpool defence that looks futureproof
text: The feeling at Liverpool is the future of central defence is bright -- and Giovanni Leoni's return later this month will strengthen it further.The 19-year-old Italian moved to Anfield with a growing reputation as one of the brightest prospects in world football. Since then, the arrival of fellow rising stars Jeremy Jacquet (21), Ifeanyi Ndukwe (18) and Mor Talla Ndiaye (18) have bolstered the youthful side of the defensive department. There has also been the arrival of the more experienced Ronald Araujo, who may have his loan spell from Barcelona turned into a permanent move.Behind the scenes, according to people with knowledge of the situation, who, like all of those spoken to for this article have been kept anonymous to protect relationships, much of the excitement surrounds the slightly older and more experienced Jacquet. There is interest in just how far his potential can take him after making an impressive start to life in the Premier League alongside skipper Virgil van Dijk.Yet it's Leoni's expected return to full training in a fortnight after over 12 months out with an anterior cruciate ligament injury in his left knee that will bring a new dimension to a department that is now starting to look in great shape.Liverpool's plan for Leoni when he arrived from Parma for an initial fee of £26million in August 2025 was clear. First, he would be slowly integrated into the team, either alongside Van Dijk or the now-departed Ibrahima Konate, to see whether he had the capabilities of replacing either starting centre-back in the long term.The first impressions were good on his debut against Southampton in the Carabao Cup. He put in a commanding performance in the heart of defence and showed maturity beyond his tender years until sustaining the horrific injury late in the game after an awkward fall.There is no modern-day Anfield story quite like it. Philipp Degen broke two ribs on his competitive debut in 2008 but missed only two months, and even when Antonio Nunez twisted his left knee on the first day of training after signing for Rafa Benitez in August 2004, he recovered and returned to play within three months.Sources say that, while Leoni has spent a year on the sidelines and understandably endured some difficult days, he has never let his focus slip. He chose to complete his rehabilitation at the AXA Training Centre, unlike others who have returned to more comfortable surroundings when out for so long, as he wanted to build stronger relationships with staff.He used the time wisely to understand more about Liverpool and improve his English, according to sources. His strong mentality and attitude have subsequently been well received, and there's a genuine respect from performance and medical staff for how he handled the setback of the injury and the dedication he showed during a gruelling rehabilitation programme.The positive for the 6ft 5in towering defender is that, even though he would have played regularly last season, time is still on his side and, most crucially, the dark days are now behind him. The hope is that he returns to full training in the week commencing October 12.Born into a sporty family of giants, Leoni has always been blessed with size and strength, but the extra work in the gym has added a new dimension to his physicality -- and soon Liverpool may be reaping the benefit.His training plan has been staggered up until this point, and careful consideration will follow in the weeks ahead. Under-21 games may present an opportunity to build up confidence and match fitness as the first-team prepare for 10 games across 28 days from October 11, but there's no need to rush him back and the EFL Trophy clash at Doncaster on Tuesday (October 7) will come too soon.Leoni will be afforded the time he needs to catch up and, with Jacquet settling nicely into the right-sided central role, Joe Gomez back in the picture and Araujo building up his integration in the team as a makeshift right-back, Liverpool's defensive options are strong.Of course, sources say, he's itching for a return after waiting so patiently to make an impact, but after such a testing period he understands the need to maintain patience as the light at the end of the tunnel brightens.This three-week international break will help as Leoni learns more about the requirements of playing under Andoni Iraola, the head coach who tried to sign him for Bournemouth before Liverpool pounced.As an aggressive centre-back who is dominant in the air and also blessed with exceptional recovery speed, Leoni fits into the mould of defenders Iraola likes.Admittedly, this half of the season may be more about settling into the demands of Premier League football, having only made 17 senior appearances for Parma before a big-money move. Building on-pitch connections with those around him will be key for the remainder of the campaign, especially as Van Dijk and Gomez are both out of contract at the end of the season and the future of the rearguard could be heavily weighted towards those with the potential to step up.There's no doubting the belief Liverpool have in him alongside Jacquet, but the real challenge will begin if Van Dijk departs and the responsibility falls on young shoulders. At the start of next season, the pair will be 22 and 20 respectively which, as exciting as it sounds, also feels incredibly young. That both Ndukwe, currently on loan at Levante, and Ndiaye have also been earmarked as centre-backs with the potential to feature in the first-team may help the rebuilding process.In the space of two transfer windows between the summer of 2025 and the start of 2026, Liverpool acted with conviction. They beat strong competition to convince Leoni and Jacquet that the short-term future was theirs. Sources say they also reassured Ndukwe and Ndiaye through persuasive video calls, presentations and family meetings that a separate pathway was in place if they chose Anfield as their next destination.It may not work out for all four, but in time it could also be the making of the next generation.This article originally appeared in The Athletic.

He chose to complete his rehabilitation at the AXA Training Centre, unlike others who have returned to more comfortable surroundings when out for so long, as he wanted to build stronger relationships with staff.He used the time wisely to understand more about Liverpool and improve his English, according to sources.
